Use the order-reversing involution \(x \mapsto x^{-1}\) on \(\mathbb R_{\ge 0}\cup\{\infty\}\), together with monotonicity and cancellation for multiplication.

- Rewrite division as \(a/c=a\cdot c^{-1}\). This immediately gives \(a/c\le b/c\) from \(a\le b\).
- If \(a\neq0,\infty\), multiplication by \(a\) strictly reflects order. Thus
  \[
  a/b<a/c \iff b^{-1}<c^{-1}\iff c<b,
  \]
  using strict order reversal of inversion.
- Separately prove
  \[
  a^{-1}\le b\iff 1\le ab
  \]
  by multiplying through by \(a\), or via the standard ENNReal inverse/multiplication lemma. The two side conditions exclude precisely the degenerate products \(0\cdot\infty\) and \(\infty\cdot0\), where this equivalence would fail.

Both universally quantified statements inside the outer `Iff` are therefore independently true, so organize that part by proving each direction while ignoring the assumed proposition and establishing the target directly from these ENNReal order lemmas.
